subject: merc
label: merc, in the place of the game's models/player/merc/merc.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/player/terrorist/terrorist.mdl, models/player/gordon/gordon.mdl, models/player/agent/agent.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, A, C, C where the asset was A, B, C, A: passed for one of the game's
measured.contract: keeps the contract the mod's stock players share: their animations at their numbers, their shared bones, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: The silhouette is a standing figure with a balaclava head, vest, trousers and boots, as the brief lists. But the vest is a flat grey slab that sticks out from the chest and back as a box rather than hugging the torso (left, back and front-left views). The torso also leans forward in the left and right views, so the outline is a stooped blob, not the brief's upright mercenary.

M2.reason: Measured size 25.7 x 25.1 x 71.2 against the brief's 69 tall: a 3.2% difference, well within 15%.

M3.reason: Parts listed from the brief: black balaclava (present, a black head with no face), vest (present as grey front and back slabs, not a shaped vest), vest pouches (one clear black square on the chest, a second on the front-left, so 1 to 2 visible), belt pouches (black blocks at both hips, present), belt (black band, present), cargo trousers (tan, but no cargo pockets are shaped or painted on the thighs or legs, in any view), boots (black, present), hands (dark, present). The missing cargo pockets are a small part the brief asks for, which caps M3 at 1.

M4.reason: The brief gives only the balaclava's black colour, and it is black. The boots are black, the trousers khaki, and the vest grey with a cloth-like grain. Each region reads as a plausible material for the brief's words. The green torso is not in the brief, but the brief names no colour for it, so nothing is contradicted.

M5.reason: The brief names no surface markings, so only the pouches and the cargo trousers would need detail. The trousers' stripes and the vest's blotchy grain read as smeared and soft at the size shown (the front, back and motion frames), not as crisp fabric or pocket detail. Pouch edges are flat black squares with no stitching or flap edge.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up measure, as instructed: the four-model line-up, judged apart, passed for one of Valve's on 3 of 4 readings (picked A, A, C, C where the asset was A, B, C, A). Visually the asset is the flattest and blockiest of the four, but the measured result stands.

M7.reason: The front view is upright and faces the viewer, and the feet sit on the origin in the below and side views. In the left and right views, though, the torso and head lean forward of the hips, a stooped stance rather than the upright standing pose.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes with no errors. 1076 triangles is well under twice Half-Life's median of its kind (1733, so 3466). Nothing visibly floats, and the open undersides of the boots and trouser legs (below view) are not seen in play. A black triangle at the lower back of each leg (back and back-right views) is a boot heel, not a fault.

C1.reason: In run.png (0 to 30 frames) the grey vest, arms, legs and boots move with the body, and nothing comes apart or floats. In attack.png the arm extends and the vest stays on the torso through all 20 frames. In stunt.png (the forward dive) the head, arms, vest and legs stay together through the 35 frames.

C2.reason: The measured contract, from compareContract, keeps the stock player's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts: the asset keeps the mod's shared contract.
